topics.label: Introduction to cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss standard cancer treatments, including surgical resection, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents along with their mechanisms and limitations.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit cancer-specific vulnerabilities, such as hormone receptor reliance, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeting oncogene addiction and kinase inhibitor therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the targeting of hyperactivated kinases driven by oncogene addiction and the subsequent development of drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are engineered to selectively target tumor cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and various immunotherapies, including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical trends, and future perspectives in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on clinical challenges, historical survival trends, ethical considerations regarding quality of life, and the future trajectory of cancer management.
